implementation_notes: Python messaging clients expose the AMQP property directly: pika declares an exclusive callback queue (queue_declare(queue='', exclusive=True)), publishes pika.BasicProperties(reply_to=callback_queue, correlation_id=...), and the worker answers with routing_key=props.reply_to. Celery raises the same field to task level (apply_async(..., reply_to=...) or a reply_to header) and maps it onto BasicProperties.reply_to with the task id as correlation id, which is the idiomatic way to divert a task's result to a callback queue instead of the result backend.
idiom_name: AMQP reply_to property (pika) / Celery reply_to option
code_sketch:
result = channel.queue_declare(queue='', exclusive=True)
callback_queue = result.method.queue
channel.basic_publish('', 'rpc_queue', request, properties=pika.BasicProperties(
    reply_to=callback_queue, correlation_id=corr_id))

def on_request(ch, method, props, body):
    ch.basic_publish('', routing_key=props.reply_to,   # the return address
                     properties=pika.BasicProperties(correlation_id=props.correlation_id),
                     body=str(fib(int(body))))
    ch.basic_ack(delivery_tag=method.delivery_tag)
pitfalls: A per-request callback queue is expensive and pika's BlockingConnection is not thread-safe: prefer one callback queue per client and match on correlation_id.
Messages whose correlation_id is unknown must be discarded (a redelivered request can produce a duplicate reply), never raised on.
Closing the connection deletes the exclusive callback queue, so any in-flight request will find no address to answer.
